# OrangeDeck

> Bitcoin mempool visualizer for Linux, Windows and Android, with a block height clock, Bitaxe monitor, block explorer and market data. Free and open source.

OrangeDeck is a free desktop and Android application that draws the Bitcoin mempool as a living tile mosaic. It combines six views in one window: mempool feed, block height clock, mining figures, block explorer, market data and watch-only addresses. It runs on Linux, Windows and Android and as a DankMaterialShell plugin, speaks thirteen languages, is MIT licensed and requires no account.

Current version: 0.2.13, released 2026-09-25. Website: https://orangedeck.dev/en/

## Six views

- **Feed**: The mempool as a living mosaic, with the last block beside it. Colour by age, fee or transaction type.
- **Clock**: Block height, fees, price, hashrate and the halving countdown, large and without controls. For a tablet on the wall.
- **Mining**: A Bitaxe monitor: hashrate, best share against the network difficulty, temperature and power of your own miner. Beside it the network with hashrate, difficulty and the next adjustment.
- **Explorer**: Search by height, hash, txid or address. Browse blocks and their contents, see what replaced what.
- **Market**: Price as candles or a line, volume, cumulative volume delta and liquidations, aggregated across exchanges.
- **Wallet**: Your own addresses or an xpub, watch-only. Your transactions are highlighted while they sit in the heap. Needs the OrangeDeck service on a Linux computer; phones and Windows reach it over the home network.

## Where it runs

- **Any Linux desktop**: An ordinary window. Wayland with an X11 fallback.
- **As a widget or bar**: Layer-shell on niri, sway, Hyprland, river, labwc.
- **Inside DankMaterialShell**: Listed in the DMS plugin directory. As a dashboard tab, a bar pill, a control center tile or a desktop widget.
- **Windows**: A ZIP, unzip and run. The same views; the wallet comes from a service on a Linux computer in the same network.
- **macOS**: Builds, but has not been tested yet. There is no package so far.
- **Android**: Phone or tablet. Each view has its own home screen shortcut.

## Where the numbers come from

- **Blocks, mempool, fees, hashrate**: The public WebSocket of mempool.space, or your own mempool instance. That is one setting.
- **Price and trades**: The public streams of Binance, Bybit and OKX.
- **Liquidations**: Bybit and OKX. The heatmap is a model built from Binance open interest, and it says so on screen.
- **Your own miner**: The local API of the device, AxeOS or cgminer. The request stays in your home network.
- **Watched addresses**: Balance queries to the same mempool instance. No keys, and nothing else leaves the device.

## Get it

- **Windows**: Version 0.2.13. ZIP for Windows 10 and 11, 64-bit: unzip and run orangedeck-app.exe. Not signed, SmartScreen asks on the first start. https://github.com/orangedeck-dev/orangedeck/releases/latest/download/orangedeck-0.2.13-windows-x86_64.zip
- **Linux**: Version 0.2.13. Flatpak bundle: flatpak install --user orangedeck-0.2.13.flatpak. The runtime comes from Flathub. https://github.com/orangedeck-dev/orangedeck/releases/latest/download/orangedeck-0.2.13.flatpak
- **DankMaterialShell**: From the DMS plugin directory: dms plugins install orangedeck. Runs on its own and uses the app's data when the app is running. https://github.com/orangedeck-dev/dms-plugin
- **Android APK**: Version 0.2.13. For Android 9 or newer, 64-bit ARM. Signed, the release notes give the fingerprint. https://github.com/orangedeck-dev/orangedeck/releases/latest/download/orangedeck-0.2.13-arm64-v8a.apk
- **F-Droid**: OrangeDeck's own repository. Add it once in F-Droid, Droid-ify or Neo Store, and updates arrive by themselves. https://fdroid.orangedeck.dev/repo/
- **Obtainium**: Takes every new version straight from the GitHub releases. Add the repository address as the source. https://github.com/orangedeck-dev/orangedeck
- **All versions**: Release notes, checksums and older versions on GitHub. https://github.com/orangedeck-dev/orangedeck/releases
- **Source**: Build it yourself. MIT. https://github.com/orangedeck-dev/orangedeck

## More about OrangeDeck

- [A Bitaxe monitor next to the mempool](https://orangedeck.dev/en/bitaxe/): Watch your Bitaxe or any AxeOS or cgminer device: hashrate, best share against the network difficulty, temperature and power. Local, free, no account.
- [A block height display for the wall](https://orangedeck.dev/en/wall-display/): Turn an old Android tablet into a Bitcoin block height display: block height, fees, price, Moscow time and the halving countdown in large figures. Free, no account.
- [OrangeDeck in DankMaterialShell](https://orangedeck.dev/en/dankmaterialshell/): OrangeDeck as a DankMaterialShell plugin: mempool feed, block height clock, mining, explorer and market in a bar popout, plus a desktop widget. One command to install.
- [What's new](https://orangedeck.dev/en/changelog/): Release history of OrangeDeck, the Bitcoin mempool visualizer: what changed in each version, with dates.

## Questions

### Does it need my keys?

No. It cannot sign anything. Watched addresses are entered as addresses or an xpub and never leave your machine except as a balance query.

### Where does the data come from?

From mempool.space by default, or from your own mempool instance. That is a single setting. Market data comes from the exchanges' public feeds.

### Does it phone home?

No. There is no server of ours, no analytics and no crash reporting.

### What does it cost?

Nothing. It is MIT licensed and there is no paid tier.

### Which languages does it speak?

Thirteen: English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese (Portugal and Brazil), Dutch, Russian, Japanese, Chinese, Polish and Czech. It starts in the system language, and numbers and dates follow the language you pick in the settings.

### Is the liquidation heatmap real data?

No, and it says so on screen. Nobody publishes other people's positions; it is a model with its assumptions written out.

### Can I run it on a tablet on the wall?

That is what the clock view is for: large figures, no controls. The Android build carries a shortcut straight into it.

### Which miners does OrangeDeck support?

AxeOS devices such as the Bitaxe and NerdAxe, and miners with the cgminer API, for example Antminer, Avalon and Whatsminer.

### Does the miner data leave my network?

No. OrangeDeck asks the device directly at its local address. Nothing goes through a server.

### Can I watch several miners?

Yes. Enter the addresses in the settings, separated by a vertical bar, for example http://192.168.1.42|http://192.168.1.43.

### Does the screen stay on?

Yes, on Android while the app is in fullscreen. When you leave fullscreen or switch apps, the normal screen timeout applies again.

### Which tablets work?

Android 9 or newer with a 64-bit ARM processor. That covers most tablets from the last years.

### Do I need my own node?

No. The numbers come from mempool.space. If you run your own mempool instance, enter its address and the clock uses that.

### Which DMS version is needed?

DankMaterialShell 1.5.0 or newer, on any compositor that DMS supports.

### Do I need the OrangeDeck app as well?

No. The plugin fetches everything itself. With the app and its service running, it shares their connection.

### Where is the source?

In its own repository, github.com/orangedeck-dev/dms-plugin, generated from the main project. MIT licensed.

## Origin

The tile packing and colour model are ports from bitfeed (MIT, mononaut).
OrangeDeck itself is MIT licensed, copyright 2026 Satoshoe.
